scenarios.title: Running late for dinner
scenarios.situation: You're stuck on a delayed bus and need to tell Sarah you'll be late for dinner with her parents.
details: the bus is stuck near the central station
delivery: change your mind about the time halfway: first say twenty minutes, then say more like half an hour

scenarios.title: Boiler still broken
scenarios.situation: You're writing to Mr. Levin, your landlord, because the boiler he promised to fix last week is still not working.
details: you can be home Thursday morning
delivery: start one sentence, abandon it, and restart it differently
repeat the point about no hot water near the end

scenarios.title: Ideas after the client call
scenarios.situation: You just got off a call with Tom about a client pitch and want to capture your thoughts before you forget them.
details: the client wants a shorter video
ask Tom about the stock footage licence
delivery: someone knocks at the door partway through: say 'one sec, come in, thanks' to them, then carry on

scenarios.title: Weekly project update
scenarios.situation: You're dictating the weekly status update for your team: what got done, what slipped, and what's next.
details: the website launch moved to next Monday
Tom is on leave Wednesday to Friday
the analytics dashboard is still blocked
delivery: cover at least three distinct topics so paragraph breaks are natural
lose your train of thought once and recover

scenarios.title: Shopping list for the weekend
scenarios.situation: You're adding to the shared shopping list before you head out.
delivery: say it as you'd naturally say it, not as a numbered list
